details: Geopolitical developments concerning US-Iran relations, including discussions around a ceasefire proposal, have led to heightened volatility in cryptocurrency markets. Data indicates approximately $120 million in long positions were liquidated within the past 24 hours. The overall market sentiment, as reflected by the Crypto Fear & Greed Index, has shifted from 'Greed' to 'Neutral'. European stock markets also experienced a downturn, as hopes for an imminent resolution to the Iran conflict waned, and concerns regarding oil supply disruptions persisted.
title: Middle East Tensions Drive Crypto Market Volatility & Liquidations

details: On April 23, the Council of the European Union adopted its 20th package of restrictive measures against Russia. This package includes a comprehensive ban on providers and platforms established in Russia that facilitate the transfer and exchange of crypto assets. Additionally, transactions in the cryptocurrency RUBx and any EU support for the development of the digital ruble are now prohibited.
title: EU Imposes New Sanctions, Bans Russian Crypto Transfers

details: Europe's securities regulator, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), has warned that the risks and potential speed of cyberattacks are increasing, partly due to rapidly evolving Artificial Intelligence (AI) models. Geopolitical tensions are cited as a factor amplifying these cybersecurity risks. ESMA is actively engaging with supervised financial entities to assess their defenses against these emerging threats.
title: Europe's Markets Watchdog Warns of Growing AI-Driven Cyber Threats

details: The Trump administration has implemented new measures aimed at preventing Chinese developers from utilizing American AI models. This move is expected to further strain US-China relations, and prediction markets indicate increased skepticism regarding a potential visit by former President Trump to China in the near future due to heightened diplomatic friction.
title: US Escalates AI Restrictions on China, Heightening Tensions

details: The US Department of Justice, as part of its "Scam Center Strike Force," announced significant actions against Southeast Asian criminal organizations perpetrating cryptocurrency investment fraud. These measures include charging two Chinese nationals, restraining over $700 million in cryptocurrency, and seizing more than 500 scam websites. The Treasury Department also imposed sanctions on individuals and entities involved in these fraud schemes, which utilized forced labor in Cambodia.
title: US Justice Department Takes Major Action Against Crypto Scam Centers
